[docs/resource-guides/digitalocean/storage.md#digitalocean-spaces-bucket-type-storage]
Read and write objects in a Spaces bucket (S3-compatible) from a handler. **Not supported on DigitalOcean:** `storage` triggers. To run code when objects arrive, list the bucket from a `schedule` function, or watch it from the [on-premises host](../../resources.md#storage-drivers) with `driver: spaces`.

[docs/resource-guides/digitalocean/topic.md#digitalocean-managed-kafka-topic-type-topic]
Publish to (or read from) a topic in a Managed Kafka cluster from a handler. **Not supported on DigitalOcean:** `topic` triggers. Consume from a `schedule` function, or from the [on-premises host](../../resources.md#custom-drivers) with a `custom` Kafka driver class ([`examples/19-custom-drivers`](../../../examples/19-custom-drivers) has a Kafka template).

[docs/resource-guides/gcp/custom.md#other-google-cloud-services-type-custom]
`custom` is for any service that isn't a bucket, queue, topic, database or cache: Firestore, Secret Manager, BigQuery, Vertex AI, a third-party API. pskit only passes its details to your functions (`external: true` is required). Google Cloud client libraries authenticate as the function's service account, so most services need **no keys**: grant the runtime service account a role, and put names and IDs in `connection`.

[docs/resource-guides/gcp/database.md#cloud-sql-type-database]
pskit's Cloud Functions don't run in a VPC, so the simplest path is a **public IP** instance reached through the **Cloud SQL Python Connector**: it authenticates with the function's service account and encrypts the connection, with no authorized networks to open. A private-IP-only instance needs a Serverless VPC Access connector, added as shown in [cache.md](cache.md#3-declare-it-in-pskityml).
